title: Dual-Parameter Synergy-Sensitivity Profiling of Epigenetic-Targeted Drug Combinations in Cancer
description: Combination therapies improve cancer outcomes but remain limited by unpredictable drug-drug interactions. Epigenetic-targeted agents can resensitize tumors to targeted drugs, yet the synergistic versus antagonistic landscape of such pairs is incompletely mapped. Here, we systematically scored 1,151 epigenetic-targeted drug-pair dose-response blocks (each block is one drug pair assessed under one experimental condition) drawn from the ALMANAC and CLOUD datasets aggregated in DrugCombDB, using a dual-parameter computational framework. Synergy was quantified with four reference models (HSA, Bliss, Loewe, ZIP) on publicly available dose-response matrices, and therapeutic utility was scored with the Combination Sensitivity Score (CSS). Of 506 unanimously classified blocks, 36 (3.1% of all blocks; 7.1% of unanimous) were synergistic, 171 (14.9%; 33.8%) were antagonistic, and 299 (26.0%; 59.1%) fell within the additive range; the remaining 645 blocks (56.0%) showed model-discordant signs and were treated as indeterminate. Synergy was determined by the partner rather than by the epigenetic class: with the HDAC inhibitor romidepsin held fixed, per-partner synergistic fractions spanned 100% (gefitinib, fulvestrant) to 0% (dasatinib, ruxolitinib, nilotinib, sunitinib, vismodegib). No enrichment was observed for HDAC inhibitor-containing pairs after composition adjustment (Fisher p=0.0025). A dual-parameter filter (synergy >5 and CSS >50%) reclassified 13 of 36 (36.1%) consensus-synergistic blocks as sensitivity-insufficient and flagged 35 antagonistic blocks (20.5%) that sensitivity-only screening would prioritize, demonstrating that integrating four synergy models with sensitivity scoring provides a pragmatic roadmap for prioritizing epigenetic-targeted combinations and avoiding antagonistic regimens in preclinical development.
